title: 3Sum
source: canonical 3Sum concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of integers nums. Return every unique triplet [a, b, c] of values from three different positions with a + b + c == 0. Each triplet must be listed in ascending order, and the list of triplets itself must be sorted in ascending order. The same triplet of values must not appear twice.

examples.explanation: Each triplet uses three different positions and sorts to a sum of 0.
The only triplet of values from three different positions that sums to 0 is -3, 1, 2.

hints: Fix one value and the problem collapses to finding two later values with a known sum.
Sorting first groups duplicates together and lets a pair search run with two converging pointers, like Two Sum II.
After sorting: for each i (skipping repeated values), sweep left = i+1 and right = end inward, recording zero sums and skipping duplicate values on both sides.
solution: Sort the array. For each index i, run the Two Sum II converging-pointer sweep on the suffix for target -nums[i], appending each zero sum once. Skipping duplicate values at all three positions keeps the output unique and already ascending: O(n^2) time after the O(n log n) sort, O(1) extra space besides the output.
